title: Ibrance (palbociclib): Practical Prescribing Guide for US Healthcare Providers
subtitle: Approved Use, Patient Selection, Dosing, Monitoring, Efficacy, and Balanced Safety
audience: US Healthcare Providers (oncology/hematology clinicians) prescribing or considering Ibrance (palbociclib) for HR-positive breast cancer

slides.title: Welcome and Learning Objectives
slides.purpose: Set expectations and outline objectives for this HCP education session on Ibrance (palbociclib).
content: Review current FDA-approved indications and mechanism of action for Ibrance (palbociclib)
Discuss patient selection, dosing, administration, and monitoring requirements per current label
Summarize pivotal efficacy data (progression-free and overall survival) across approved combination regimens
Review key safety information: neutropenia, interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis, embryo-fetal toxicity
Identify essential patient counseling points to support safe, effective use

slides.title: Disease Rationale for CDK4/6 Inhibition
slides.purpose: Establish the biological rationale for combining a CDK4/6 inhibitor with endocrine therapy in HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer.
content: HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer accounts for approximately 65-70% of all breast cancers
Dysregulated cyclin D-CDK4/6-retinoblastoma (Rb) pathway signaling drives proliferation in this subtype

Endocrine therapy plus a CDK4/6 inhibitor is described in clinical education literature as the guideline-recommended first-line approach for HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced/metastatic breast cancer

slides.title: Mechanism of Action
slides.purpose: Explain how palbociclib works to support clinical rationale for use.
content: Palbociclib is a selective, oral, reversible inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6 (CDK4/6)
Cyclin D1 and CDK4/6 lie downstream of proliferative signaling pathways; inhibition blocks retinoblastoma (Rb) protein phosphorylation and arrests cells in G1 phase
In vitro, palbociclib reduced proliferation of estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer cell lines by blocking progression from G1 into S phase
Combining palbociclib with antiestrogens increased growth arrest and cell senescence compared with either agent alone

slides.title: Current FDA-Approved Indications
slides.purpose: Clarify approved combination regimens and patient populations to ensure on-label use.
content: With an aromatase inhibitor as initial endocrine-based therapy for HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer
With fulvestrant for HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer following disease progression on endocrine therapy

With inavolisib and fulvestrant for endocrine-resistant, PIK3CA-mutated HR-positive, HER2-negative disease (mutation detected by an FDA-approved test), following recurrence on or after adjuvant endocrine therapy
With trastuzumab, with or without pertuzumab, and endocrine therapy for maintenance treatment of HR-positive, HER2-positive advanced or metastatic breast cancer following induction treatment

slides.title: Patient Selection Considerations
slides.purpose: Guide appropriate patient identification consistent with the current label.
content: Confirm HR-positive status (and HER2-negative or HER2-positive status, as applicable to the intended regimen) using validated biomarker testing before initiating therapy
For the inavolisib combination, confirm a PIK3CA mutation using an FDA-approved test
Approved for adult men and women; population pharmacokinetic data show no clinically important effect of age, gender, or body weight on drug exposure

No dose adjustment is required for mild or moderate hepatic impairment, or for renal impairment with creatinine clearance greater than 15 mL/min; dose reduction is required for severe hepatic impairment

slides.title: Dosing and Administration
slides.purpose: Reinforce correct dosing schedule and administration technique to support adherence and safety.
content: Recommended starting dose: 125 mg orally once daily for 21 consecutive days followed by 7 days off treatment (a complete 28-day cycle)
Capsules must be taken with food; tablets may be taken with or without food
Swallow capsules/tablets whole; do not chew, crush, open, or split; do not take if broken or cracked
If a dose is vomited or missed, do not take an additional dose that day; resume the next scheduled dose at the usual time
Encourage patients to take their dose at approximately the same time each day

slides.title: Dose Modification and Drug Interactions
slides.purpose: Support safe co-prescribing and proactive toxicity management.
content: For severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class C), reduce the dose to 75 mg once daily on the same 21-days-on/7-days-off schedule
Avoid concomitant strong CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole) and strong CYP3A inducers (e.g., rifampin); avoid grapefruit or grapefruit juice during treatment
Dose interruption, dose reduction, or delay in starting a treatment cycle is recommended for patients who develop Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia, based on individual safety and tolerability

slides.title: Efficacy: First-Line Setting (PALOMA-2)
slides.purpose: Present primary efficacy evidence supporting the aromatase inhibitor combination.
content: Phase 3 PALOMA-2 randomized 666 postmenopausal women with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer and no prior therapy for advanced disease to palbociclib plus letrozole or placebo plus letrozole
Primary endpoint met: median progression-free survival 24.8 months vs 14.5 months with palbociclib plus letrozole vs placebo plus letrozole

Final overall survival analysis (90-month median follow-up): numerically longer OS (53.9 vs 51.2 months) that was not statistically significant (HR 0.956; 95% CI, 0.777-1.177); OS was a secondary endpoint and the trial was not powered to detect an OS difference

slides.title: Efficacy: Endocrine-Resistant Setting (PALOMA-3)
slides.purpose: Present efficacy evidence supporting the fulvestrant combination after prior endocrine therapy.
content: Phase 3 PALOMA-3 enrolled 521 patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer whose disease progressed after prior endocrine therapy, randomized to palbociclib plus fulvestrant or placebo plus fulvestrant
Primary endpoint met: median progression-free survival 9.5 months vs 4.6 months with palbociclib plus fulvestrant vs placebo plus fulvestrant (HR 0.46; 95% CI, 0.36-0.59)
A long-term exploratory overall survival analysis (73.3-month median follow-up) showed median OS of 34.8 vs 28.0 months (HR 0.81; 95% CI, 0.65-0.99); OS was a secondary/exploratory endpoint

slides.title: Newer Approved Combinations: Expanding the Evidence Base
slides.purpose: Familiarize HCPs with the two most recently approved palbociclib combination regimens.
content: INAVO120: inavolisib plus palbociclib plus fulvestrant vs placebo plus palbociclib plus fulvestrant in endocrine-resistant, PIK3CA-mutated HR-positive, HER2-negative disease; median progression-free survival 15.0 vs 7.3 months

PATINA: palbociclib plus trastuzumab (with or without pertuzumab) plus endocrine therapy vs trastuzumab (with or without pertuzumab) plus endocrine therapy alone, as maintenance after induction therapy in HR-positive, HER2-positive advanced/metastatic breast cancer; investigator-assessed progression-free survival hazard ratio 0.76 (95% CI, 0.59-0.97)
Overall survival data for the PATINA maintenance regimen remain immature; follow-up is ongoing

slides.title: Safety: Neutropenia (Most Common Adverse Reaction)
slides.purpose: Equip HCPs to anticipate, monitor, and manage the most frequent adverse reaction.
content: Neutropenia was the most frequently reported adverse reaction: 80% of patients in PALOMA-2 and 83% in PALOMA-3 (any grade), with Grade 3 or 4 decreases in the majority of these cases
Median time to first episode of any-grade neutropenia was 15 days; median duration of Grade 3 or higher neutropenia was 7 days; the effect is not cumulative across cycles
Monitor complete blood count prior to starting therapy, at the beginning of each cycle, on Day 15 of the first 2 cycles, and as clinically indicated
Febrile neutropenia occurred in 1.8% of patients across PALOMA-2 and PALOMA-3; instruct patients to promptly report any fever

slides.title: Safety: ILD/Pneumonitis and Embryo-Fetal Toxicity
slides.purpose: Reinforce recognition and management of serious, less common risks.
content: Severe, life-threatening, or fatal interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis can occur; monitor patients for pulmonary symptoms such as hypoxia, cough, and dyspnea
Interrupt IBRANCE immediately for suspected ILD/pneumonitis and evaluate; permanently discontinue for severe cases; additional fatalities have been reported in the postmarketing setting

IBRANCE can cause fetal harm based on animal data and mechanism of action; advise effective contraception during treatment (females: at least 3 weeks after the last dose; males with female partners of reproductive potential: 3 months after the last dose)
The current label lists no contraindications

slides.title: Patient Counseling Essentials
slides.purpose: Provide practical talking points to support adherence and early recognition of adverse events.
content: Take at approximately the same time each day; capsules always with food, tablets with or without food
Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, and grapefruit products throughout treatment
Promptly report fever, new or worsening respiratory symptoms, or signs of infection or unusual bleeding/bruising
Use effective contraception during treatment; do not breastfeed during treatment and for 3 weeks after the last dose

slides.title: Key Takeaways and Application to Practice
slides.purpose: Consolidate learning and translate it into practical, on-label prescribing behavior.
content: Ibrance (palbociclib) combined with an aromatase inhibitor, fulvestrant, inavolisib plus fulvestrant, or trastuzumab-based therapy is FDA-approved across defined HR-positive breast cancer populations

Consistent, substantial progression-free survival benefit has been demonstrated across pivotal trials; overall survival findings vary by trial and endocrine partner and should be discussed with patients accurately
Structured complete blood count monitoring and prompt dose modification make neutropenia a manageable, largely reversible toxicity in most patients
Counsel patients on administration technique, grapefruit avoidance, contraception, and prompt reporting of fever or respiratory symptoms at every visit
